network.overall_strategy: The network is centered on the only experimentally resolved prebiotic route to the proline skeleton: the Patel-type cyanosulfidic surface sequence from HCN, acetylene, NH3, and sulfide. To correct the balance problems of earlier coarse renderings, the route is expanded into explicit aldehyde, cyanohydrin, cyclic alpha-hydroxythioamide, thiolactam, imine, and aminonitrile nodes. Three chemically motivated choice points are encoded as parallel reactions: Cu-free vs Cu-accelerated aldehyde generation, Cu-free vs Cu-accelerated photodeoxygenation to the thiolactam, and late surface-photochemical vs hydrothermal H2/FeS/NiS desulfurization to the imine. No known prebiotic chemistry makes L-proline directly; therefore the target node is reached only after hydrolysis of proline aminonitrile and seed-dependent physical enantioenrichment, with the D-proline node used as the explicit non-target companion phase. Cyanamide diversion to arginine is acknowledged in reaction reasoning but omitted as a non-target sink.

reactions.name: Cu(I)-mediated HCN-acetylene coupling to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Post-impact surface streams or evaporitic pools; acetylene supplied by carbide hydrolysis; anoxic and UV-exposed.

reactions.mechanism: Copper(I)-promoted cyanovinylation of acetylene by HCN gives acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. explicitly identify Cu(I)-catalyzed cross-coupling of HCN and acetylene to acrylonitrile as the entry to the proline branch (Patel et al., 2015). This is the best-supported carbon-skeleton entry, although Cu availability and acetylene delivery to surface waters remain geochemically contested (Ranjan et al., 2018; Todd et al., 2024).

reactions.name: Aza-Michael addition of ammonia to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Ammonia-rich shallow pool or stream; near-neutral to mildly alkaline.

reactions.mechanism: NH3 adds conjugatively to the activated C=C bond of acrylonitrile to give beta-aminopropionitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. describe NH3 addition to acrylonitrile as the direct precursor step into the proline branch (Patel et al., 2015). The reaction is chemically reasonable without a catalyst in concentrated ammonia-bearing surface waters; cyanamide is omitted here because it diverts flux toward the arginine branch rather than the target.

reactions.name: Net UV-sulfidic reduction of beta-aminopropionitrile to 3-aminopanal

conditions.other: UV-irradiated sulfidic pool; H2 is written as the net bookkeeping reductant for an atom-balanced representation of Patel UV/HS-/H2S photoreduction.

reactions.mechanism: Net two-electron reduction of the nitrile to the aldehyde level with hydrolytic release of NH3.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. use UV/H2S-driven reductive homologation to move nitriles to the aldehyde level before HCN re-addition; here that bundled chemistry is separated into an explicit aldehyde-forming node (Patel et al., 2015). H2 is used only as a bookkeeping reductant for mass balance in the graph; experimentally the reducing equivalents come from sulfidic photochemistry rather than direct low-temperature hydrogenation.

reactions.name: Cu-photoredox-accelerated net reduction of beta-aminopropionitrile to 3-aminopanal

conditions.other: UV-irradiated sulfidic pool; same net stoichiometry as rxn_003, but with Cu photoredox acceleration.

reactions.mechanism: Photoredox-accelerated net reduction of the nitrile to the aldehyde level with hydrolytic release of NH3.
reactions.reasoning: This is the Cu-accelerated variant of the Patel aldehyde-generation step; Patel et al. state that Cu(I)-Cu(II) photoredox cycling accelerates the UV/H2S network (Patel et al., 2015). The chemistry is better supported kinetically than geochemically, because Cu-rich settings are patchier and more contested than sulfide availability alone (Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: HCN addition to 3-aminopanal to form the proline-branch cyanohydrin

conditions.other: HCN-bearing pool; aldehyde capture should compete effectively at moderate HCN activity.

reactions.mechanism: The amino aldehyde undergoes Strecker-type cyanohydrin formation by HCN addition.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. place HCN addition after reduction to the amino aldehyde, giving the cyanohydrin that feeds sulfur incorporation (Patel et al., 2015). Writing this step explicitly avoids the earlier unbalanced bundling and makes clear where the extra carbon of the proline skeleton enters.

reactions.name: H2S-driven thioamidation and cyclization to the cyclic alpha-hydroxythioamide

conditions.other: Sulfidic surface water; intramolecular ring closure accompanies sulfur incorporation.

reactions.mechanism: Hydrosulfide converts the nitrile to a thioamide, followed by intramolecular cyclization to the five-membered cyclic alpha-hydroxythioamide with NH3 loss.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. report alpha-hydroxythioamides from the cyanohydrin plus H2S and note that the cyclic alpha-hydroxythioamide forms in the proline branch (Patel et al., 2015). The cyclic product is the chemically relevant precursor because it feeds directly into gamma-butyrothiolactam formation.

reactions.name: Net photodeoxygenation of the cyclic alpha-hydroxythioamide to gamma-butyrothiolactam

conditions.other: UV-exposed sulfidic pool; H2 again represents the net reducing equivalents for an atom-balanced graph representation.

reactions.mechanism: Net reductive deoxygenation of the alpha-hydroxyl group gives the cyclic thioamide gamma-butyrothiolactam.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. identify gamma-butyrothiolactam as the only deoxygenated thioamide from this branch (Patel et al., 2015). As in rxn_003, the explicit H2 bookkeeping is used to keep the network balanced while preserving the experimentally motivated UV/sulfide redox logic.

reactions.name: Cu-photoredox-accelerated net photodeoxygenation to gamma-butyrothiolactam

conditions.other: UV-irradiated sulfidic pool; same net stoichiometry as rxn_007, with Cu acceleration.

reactions.mechanism: Photoredox-accelerated net deoxygenation of the cyclic alpha-hydroxythioamide to the thiolactam.
reactions.reasoning: This is the Cu-accelerated counterpart of rxn_007, justified by Patel et al.'s broader observation that Cu(I)-Cu(II) cycling accelerates the UV/H2S reductive network (Patel et al., 2015). It remains surface-plausible only in locally Cu-enriched niches, a limitation emphasized by geochemical critiques (Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Surface reductive desulfurization of gamma-butyrothiolactam to 1-pyrroline

conditions.other: Net-balanced representation of the further Patel photoreduction; the 1-pyrroline intermediate is inferred rather than isolated.

reactions.mechanism: Reductive desulfurization/hydrogenolysis of the thiolactam generates the cyclic imine 1-pyrroline.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. report conversion of gamma-butyrothiolactam to proline aminonitrile over two further steps, with the cyclic imine best interpreted as an inferred intermediate (Patel et al., 2015). This explicit desulfurization node is therefore mechanistically motivated and improves balance, but it should be read as an inferred decomposition of the published sequence.

reactions.name: Hydrothermal FeS-NiS-assisted reductive desulfurization of gamma-butyrothiolactam to 1-pyrroline

conditions.other: H2-rich alkaline vent or subseafloor reactor; speculative late-stage handoff from a surface-generated thiolactam pool.

reactions.mechanism: Metal-sulfide-assisted hydrogenolytic desulfurization of the thiolactam to the cyclic imine.
reactions.reasoning: This branch is speculative: no prebiotic gamma-butyrothiolactam to 1-pyrroline reduction has been demonstrated. It is included because H2 with Ni- and FeS-rich systems reduces related carbonyl and imine chemistry in protometabolic work, making this a chemically plausible but untested late-stage alternative (Huber and Wachtershauser, 2003; Kitadai et al., 2019; Kaur et al., 2024).

reactions.name: HCN capture of 1-pyrroline to proline aminonitrile

conditions.other: HCN-rich surface pool; imine trapping favored before hydrolysis.

reactions.mechanism: Strecker-type addition of HCN to the cyclic iminium/imine manifold gives pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: HCN capture of the cyclic imine completes the proline aminonitrile skeleton; Patel et al. report 32% overall for the last two steps from gamma-butyrothiolactam to pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile, with the imine intermediate inferred (Patel et al., 2015). Ritson later emphasized that the cyclic proline aminonitrile is unusually resistant to retro-Strecker reversion compared with many acyclic aminonitriles, making it a plausible accumulation point (Ritson, 2021).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of proline aminonitrile with seed-dependent eutectic partition to L- and D-proline

conditions.other: Slow nitrile hydrolysis during wet-dry or geothermal cycles, followed by evaporation/crystallization or eutectic partitioning in concentrated prebiotic pools; requires a small initial L-bias from an unresolved source. mol_016 is a bookkeeping stand-in for the non-target D- or DL-rich companion phase.

reactions.mechanism: Aminonitrile hydrolysis proceeds through the usual amide/carboxyl sequence to proline; subsequent phase-behavior separation enriches one enantiomer in the recoverable solution fraction.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. stop at proline aminonitrile and do not report a hydrolysis yield to proline, so the hydrolysis half of this node is chemically necessary but experimentally unquantified in the cited cyanosulfidic system (Patel et al., 2015). The L-specific outcome is not direct asymmetric synthesis: it represents hydrolysis followed by eutectic/phase-behavior resolution, for which proline is unusually well documented, although aqueous/alcohol-relevant systems still need a seed ee and the strongest CHCl3 case is not prebiotic (Klussmann et al., 2006; Blackmond, 2019).

pathways.name: Baseline surface cyanosulfidic route
pathways.description: All redox nodes follow the non-Cu surface-photoredox representations before HCN trapping and seed-dependent recovery of an L-proline fraction.

pathways.name: Cu-assisted aldehyde-release variant
pathways.description: Cu photoredox is invoked only for the nitrile-to-aldehyde step; later thiolactam formation and imine release remain on the baseline surface route.

pathways.name: Cu-assisted thiolactam-forming variant
pathways.description: Only the alpha-hydroxythioamide-to-thiolactam conversion is assigned to the Cu-accelerated photoredox branch.

pathways.name: Fully Cu-assisted surface photoredox variant
pathways.description: Both Patel-type photoredox reductions are assigned to Cu-accelerated versions while the late desulfurization remains a surface completion step.

pathways.name: Surface-to-hydrothermal completion route
pathways.description: Surface cyanosulfidic construction is followed by a speculative hydrothermal H2/FeS/NiS desulfurization of gamma-butyrothiolactam before HCN trapping and hydrolysis/resolution.

pathways.name: Cu-assisted aldehyde generation with hydrothermal completion
pathways.description: The early nitrile-to-aldehyde step is Cu-accelerated, but the late thiolactam-to-imine conversion is shifted to the speculative hydrothermal H2/FeS/NiS branch.

pathways.name: Cu-assisted thiolactam formation with hydrothermal completion
pathways.description: Cu acceleration is used only at the alpha-hydroxythioamide deoxygenation step, followed by hydrothermal desulfurization to the imine.

pathways.name: Fully Cu-assisted mixed-environment route
pathways.description: Both surface photoredox reductions are assigned to Cu-accelerated variants, and the late desulfurization is completed hydrothermally before HCN trapping.

pathways.name: CPL-seeded fully Cu-assisted surface route
pathways.description: Chemically identical to P4, but the tiny initial L-bias required at rxn_012 is attributed to circularly polarized UV or related photonic asymmetry; the reaction backbone is unchanged.

pathways.name: Chiral-sugar or mineral-seeded mixed route
pathways.description: Chemically identical to P8, but the minimal seed ee required at rxn_012 is instead attributed to external chiral sugar transfer, stochastic fluctuation, or chiral mineral adsorption; that asymmetry source is not encoded as a separate reaction node.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Strong Patel-style surface backbone through mol_014 and good literature alignment for the proline skeleton. The main limitations are that rxn_003 and rxn_007 are encoded as H2-driven net reductions instead of explicit UV/HS-/H2S photoredox steps, rxn_009 makes the inferred 1-pyrroline intermediate a standalone surface reaction, and rxn_012 combines hydrolysis with chiral partition rather than representing them separately.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_012 explicitly as 2 mol_014 + 4 mol_005 -> mol_015 + mol_016 + 2 mol_003, or better split hydrolysis and enantioenrichment into separate steps in a prebiotic brine or eutectic setting.
Encode UV/HS-/H2S photoredox bookkeeping explicitly in rxn_003 and rxn_007 instead of H2-only shorthand.
If mol_013 is meant to remain inferred, merge rxn_009 and rxn_011 or mark rxn_009 as an inferred intermediate step.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Cu-assisted aldehyde release is consistent with the Patel framework and slightly improves the early reduction logic. Confidence is still capped by the H2 shorthand in rxn_004 and rxn_007, the inferred/desulfurization character of rxn_009, and the fact that rxn_012 only reaches L-proline as one member of a racemic or partitioned output.
suggestions: State the Cu source and loading explicitly and distinguish catalytic photoredox participation from simple net stoichiometry in rxn_004.
Split rxn_012 into hydrolysis to racemic proline plus a separate chiral amplification or partition step in a prebiotic setting.
If mol_013 is only inferred, merge rxn_009 and rxn_011 or annotate rxn_009 as inferred rather than fully established.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Cu-accelerated photodeoxygenation is literature-motivated and the sequence remains coherent to mol_014. As in P1, the net reductive bookkeeping in rxn_003 and rxn_008 is under-specified, rxn_009 is inferred rather than directly demonstrated, and rxn_012 should not merge hydrolysis with enantioenrichment.
suggestions: Make rxn_008 explicitly Cu-photoredox and sulfide-driven in the network metadata or bookkeeping.
Split rxn_012 into chemical hydrolysis and a separate prebiotic resolution step.
Consider adding racemic or R/S aminonitrile nodes if chirality is meant to be tracked downstream.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Best purely chemical surface backbone: the fully Cu-assisted Patel sequence is coherent and literature-aligned through proline aminonitrile. The remaining weaknesses are the H2 shorthand in rxn_004 and rxn_008, the inferred standalone desulfurization of rxn_009, and the under-specified final L/D separation in rxn_012.
suggestions: Keep the fully surface Patel backbone, but encode Cu and sulfide photoredox explicitly in rxn_004 and rxn_008.
Rewrite or split rxn_012 so hydrolysis and enantioenrichment are not merged into one reaction node.
If mol_013 is intended as inferred rather than isolated, merge rxn_009 and rxn_011 or annotate the imine as inferred.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The hydrothermal diversion is the dominant weakness. rxn_010 is a speculative FeS/NiS/H2 extrapolation, and the pathway then requires surface to hydrothermal to surface handling of late intermediates, with mol_013 needing to encounter HCN again in surface rxn_011 without an explicit transport justification; rxn_012 remains the same weak final step.
suggestions: Add an explicit transport or geological coupling step for moving mol_012 or mol_013 between the surface photochemical setting and the hydrothermal niche.
Treat rxn_010 as hypothetical unless direct experimental support for thiolactam desulfurization under FeS/NiS/H2 conditions is provided.
Either justify rxn_011 under hydrothermal conditions or keep the whole late stage in one environment.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Cu-assisted aldehyde generation is reasonable, but the late-stage logic is limited by the same mixed-environment problems as P5. The hydrothermal rxn_010 is weakly supported for proline, the return of mol_013 to a surface HCN pool for rxn_011 is not encoded, and rxn_012 still does not provide a clearly prebiotic route to L-proline.
suggestions: Add explicit surface to hydrothermal and hydrothermal to surface transfer rationale for the mol_012/mol_013 stage.
Provide direct literature support or downgrade rxn_010 to a speculative test reaction.
Split rxn_012 and relabel its environment as a prebiotic physical resolution setting.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The early surface chemistry is plausible, but the hydrothermal completion remains poorly supported. rxn_010 is speculative, the hydrothermal-to-surface handoff before rxn_011 is not justified for a reactive 1-pyrroline intermediate, and rxn_012 still conflates hydrolysis with physical chiral enrichment.
suggestions: Model the transport and survival of the reactive 1-pyrroline intermediate before rxn_011, or keep the late stage in one environment.
Support rxn_010 experimentally or present it as a hypothetical branch.
Separate hydrolysis from chiral amplification in rxn_012.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically ambitious but the weakest late-stage literature alignment: it combines full Cu-assisted surface photoredox with a speculative hydrothermal desulfurization. The required surface to hydrothermal to surface transfers are not modeled, and the L-proline endpoint still depends on the under-specified rxn_012.
suggestions: Simplify the late stage to one environment unless explicit transport of mol_012 or mol_013 is added.
Add stronger justification for rxn_010, which is much less supported than the Patel surface chemistry.
Split rxn_012 into hydrolysis plus a separate resolution or amplification process.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Best target-oriented variant: it preserves the literature-backed fully Cu-assisted surface backbone and at least names a plausible asymmetry source. However the CPL seed is only in the pathway label rather than an explicit node or condition set, proline-specific CPL enantioenrichment is indirect in the literature, and rxn_012 still represents racemic hydrolysis or partition more than true L-selective synthesis.
suggestions: Encode CPL exposure or seed introduction as an explicit process node with conditions and timing.
Split rxn_012 into hydrolysis to a racemic proline pool and a separate phase-behavior amplification step in an explicit prebiotic setting.
If chirality is central, represent racemic or R/S proline aminonitrile explicitly rather than a single achiral mol_014 node.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chiral sugar or mineral seeding improves the target logic, but the seed is not explicitly represented in the graph and the mixed surface/hydrothermal completion remains speculative. As in other mixed routes, rxn_010 and the unmodeled transfer into surface rxn_011 weaken the late stage, while rxn_012 should be separated into chemical hydrolysis and physical resolution.
suggestions: Represent the chiral sugar or mineral seed explicitly as a node, surface agent, or environmental condition.
Avoid the hydrothermal detour unless transport into and out of the hydrothermal compartment is justified for mol_012 or mol_013.
Split rxn_012 into chemical hydrolysis and a separate physical resolution step.

evaluation.network_feedback: Network validity is strong: the graph is connected, molecule IDs are consistent, and the RDKit check reports 0 UNBALANCED reactions. rxn_012 is not a conservation violation but is only balanceable with coefficients and should be rewritten as 2 mol_014 + 4 mol_005 -> mol_015 + mol_016 + 2 mol_003 or split into separate hydrolysis and resolution steps. Literature alignment is good through proline aminonitrile: the explicit acrylonitrile, beta-aminopropionitrile, aldehyde, cyanohydrin, cyclic alpha-hydroxythioamide, gamma-butyrothiolactam, and inferred 1-pyrroline nodes match the Patel-type cyanosulfidic backbone and correctly acknowledge that hydrolysis to proline is unquantified. The main deficits are chemical and environmental: rxn_003/004, rxn_007/008, and rxn_009/010 use H2 bookkeeping instead of explicitly encoding the cited UV/HS-/H2S redox chemistry; the Cu-accelerated variants are distinguished mostly by annotation rather than explicit catalyst metadata; rxn_010 is a speculative hydrothermal extrapolation; mixed routes require unmodeled transfer of reactive intermediates between surface and hydrothermal settings; and rxn_012 conflates chemical hydrolysis with physical enantioenrichment in a mislabeled biochemical environment. P9 and P10 also differ from P4 and P8 mostly by pathway label because the seed sources are not explicit nodes or conditions. The network therefore reaches L-proline only partially and much more convincingly reaches proline aminonitrile; if the target were proline aminonitrile rather than L-proline, confidence would be substantially higher. Best current variant is P9, but the complete L-proline network remains below the approval threshold. Consider making sulfur redox and chiral-resolution steps explicit and, if mol_013 remains only inferred, combining rxn_009 and rxn_011 into a single literature-backed late transformation with an annotated imine intermediate.
